pairs.difference: A: the shadow side of the ball stays cool lavender in the lens, there are small soft sheens on the red and blue panels, and one soft cast shadow falls right. B: a blown white hot spot sits on the upper-right panel, the lower edge turns warm with red-orange sand bounce, and the left side falls into a heavy, wide cast shadow. B's light also turns blurrily, without a clear core shadow. Both are below the real shading range, B further.
pairs.fix: Light the ball from the upper left with small soft sheens instead of a white hot spot. Keep the shadow side a cool lavender grey, with no orange glow along the bottom edge. Use one soft, short cast shadow touching the ball.

pairs.difference: A: the top bulbs throw a small pool of light onto the header underside, the backboard falls off into darkness, and the bear sits in soft shadow. B: each bulb has a big glowing halo, the target and bear are lit evenly from the front in warm clay tones, and the shelf has only faint contact shadows. Its light bias is weaker (0.33 against 0.50).
pairs.fix: Make the bulbs small with no big halos. Let light fall from above so the lower target and the bear's underside go darker. Add a soft shadow of the target onto the back panel.

pairs.difference: A: the unit has a broad soft sheen on the upper-left shoulder, a cool side panel, and a warm window patch on the wall. It is low in range (0.557). B: a hazy white bloom spreads over the wall under the vents, a dark ceiling and corner surround it, and a hard diagonal shaft crosses the wall. Light bias of 1.048 is far above the real range, a staged directional setup rather than card lighting.
pairs.fix: Remove the white haze and the dark corners. Keep the wall brightly and evenly lit with only one soft patch of window light. Shade the unit's right end a gentle cool blue.

pairs.difference: A: the chest is lit almost evenly from the front. Lid, body and coins are all warm clay in the lens, with shallow shadow and no clear shadow side, and light bias of 0.18 is below the real range. B: the lid top catches strong light and turns to a dark cool end cap, and the right side of the box falls into shadow, the light/shadow split seen on real cards.
pairs.fix: Light from the upper left so the top of the lid is bright and the right side of the chest and the lid end go a cool, darker shade. Darken the inside of the lid.

pairs.difference: A: the white crown has a broad soft sheen and the visor a long glossy streak, with a soft dark cast shadow under the left side on bright planks. B: the scene is dim and moody, with a dark room corner and a hard diagonal shadow across the back wall. The hat sits in low light with a lit warm brim underside. Both exceed the real form contrast and bias, but real cards do not sink the setting into darkness like B.
pairs.fix: Brighten the room and remove the diagonal wall shadow. Light the hat from above front with a broad soft sheen on the white crown, and keep only a soft shadow under the brim.

pairs.difference: A: the roof has a rounded sheen, the front face is bright and a long soft cast shadow falls left across a lit floor. B: the box splits hard into a dark purple left face and a cream right face, with no clear cast shadow beyond a thin dark contact line and a dark vignette around it. The real-style cool shadow side argues the other way, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Add a long soft shadow falling across the floor to one side. Soften the jump between the two faces of the booth, and remove the dark corners of the background.

pairs.difference: A: the gloves have clear broad sheens on top, dark soft cast shadows on the floor to the lower right, and shadow in the cuffs. B: the gloves are lit with blurry, even light, wide soft sheens fade into the red, the forms have little core shadow, and only a thin contact dark line sits under them. Lens values are close, so this rests on the eye.
pairs.fix: Give each glove one broad sheen at the top and a darker underside. Add a soft cast shadow on the floor falling away from the light.

pairs.difference: A: the fins have soft rounded turns, the foot pockets have a broad sheen, and edges stay soft. B: thin bright rim lines trace every fin edge and pocket lip in the lens, with sharp dark lines at the edges, the same rim tracing seen on a generated glove in the lessons. Form contrast of 0.762 is well above the real range of up to 0.605.
pairs.fix: Remove the thin bright lines along the edges. Shade the fins with soft rounded turns and one broad gentle sheen on the rubber.

pairs.difference: A: the planks and post have a clear lit top and shaded side, the pier legs go very dark at the water, and soft reflections sit below. B: pale, even daylight falls on all posts and planks, with shallow shadow under the dock and little difference between top and side faces. Light bias is 0.26 against 0.58 for A.
pairs.fix: Use one strong sun from the upper left. Brighten the plank tops, shade the post sides much darker, and put deep shadow under the dock where the legs meet the water.

pairs.difference: A: the fronds are slim with fine soft turns from pale tips to shaded blades, and the sand has only faint soft shadow. B: the fronds are thick clay shapes with dark undersides that turn abruptly, the trunk rings have banded shading, and a hard-edged purple palm shadow falls on the sand, heavier than the soft grounding on real cards.
pairs.fix: Shade the fronds with soft gradual turns, not thick dark undersides. Make the shadow on the sand faint and soft-edged, not a crisp palm shape.

pairs.difference: A: the locker is lit almost flat from the front. The side and door are the same warm tone in the lens and the interior is the only dark area. Light bias of 0.058 is far below the real range. B: light comes from one side, with a soft cast shadow on the wall and a brighter top edge, though it reads hazy.
pairs.fix: Light from the upper left so the top and left of the locker are bright and the right side falls into a darker, cooler shade. Add a soft cast shadow on the wall.

pairs.difference: A: the slide has a smooth tube turn, light glossy streaks and a soft purple-tinted cast shadow on the tiles. B: a heavy dark blue underside runs along the big curve, stark white inside, and hardly any cast shadow on the deck, with light bias of 0.149 below the real range.
pairs.fix: Add one clear sun direction with a soft cast shadow on the tiles. Lighten the underside of the slide so it stays a soft mid-tone rather than near black.

pairs.difference: A: the player is a soft rounded form with a small crisp edge sheen, a moderate darker lower-right rim, and a faint shadow on the background. B: a puffy pillow form is glowing and blurred at the edges, with a yellow-to-orange turn around the whole lower rim and a halo in the background lens, without a real cast shadow. This matches the inflated forms of generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Tighten the corners and turn the light only on the lower right, with a small soft sheen on the top corner. Remove the glow behind it and add a faint soft shadow under the player.

pairs.difference: A: the paper is flat with crisp folds, fine shadows under the flap and photos, and clear separation, with a shading range of 0.627. B: the envelope is pillowy and low in contrast, its edges dissolve into a pale haze, the photos cast barely any shadow, and it glows against the rings. Shading range is 0.447 and form contrast 0.312, both below real cards.
pairs.fix: Draw flat paper with crisp folds. Add small dark shadows under the flap and between the photos. Remove the soft glow around the envelope and deepen the shaded side.

pairs.difference: A: the plate is lit from one side, its soft cast shadow falls on the planks, and the fruit has moderate sheens. B: the bright bowl glows from within, bright caustic bands run along the rim, the fruit is lit evenly and a heavy dark band of shadow sits below it. Light bias of 0.177 is below the real range.
pairs.fix: Light the fruit from one side with a shaded far side on each piece. Use fewer highlights on the glass and a softer, lighter shadow under the bowl.

pairs.difference: A: the door, frame and wreath get even frontal light, with warm lens tones and weak shadows under leaves and frame. Light bias of 0.018 means there is almost no direction, well below the real range. The lantern glow also adds a warm patch. B: dappled leaf shadows fall across the door from the upper left and the frame shades the door strongly, giving a clear direction.
pairs.fix: Give the scene one clear light from the upper left. Cast leaf and arch shadows onto the door and wall, and darken the side of the frame turned away.

pattern: Generated cards light form in one of two ways, and neither matches the real cards' one clear sun. One is even, warm, clay-like frontal light on puffy forms: little cool shadow side, weak cast shadows and soft glow halos (p04, p11, p13, p14, p16). The other is an overstaged scene: hard shadows, dark corners, haze or thin bright rims traced along edges (p03, p05, p08, p10). Real cards keep one direction, with a cool shadow side, broad soft sheens and a soft cast shadow. Several calls are weak because the two give-aways pull in opposite directions.
